\begin{definition}[Operational shadow price, crossing bracket, and endpoint mixture]
\label{def:pi3}
Fix the implemented family's usage curve $U(w)$ on $w\ge0$ and a target $B$.

\emph{Level set.} $U^{-1}(B)=\{w\ge0:U(w)=B\}$ contains the weights that attain the target. It is empty at a usage gap and may contain a plateau.

\emph{Crossing threshold.} Suppose the curve has finitely many upward crossings of $B$ and at least one occurs at a finite weight. Define
\[
D_B=\{w\ge0:U(w)<B\text{ and some }v>w\text{ has }U(v)\ge B\}.
\]
When $D_B$ is nonempty and bounded, the operational shadow price is $w^*(B):=w^{\dagger}(B):=\sup D_B$, the final crossing location. Selecting the last crossing is a convention for nonmonotone curves. At a jump it is a single weight, even if no weight attains $B$. It is undefined if the curve never crosses from below, or has no finite final crossing. A level set can therefore exist without a shadow price.

\emph{Grid bracket.} On an ordered finite grid, let $w_{\mathrm{lo}}$ be the largest sampled weight with $U(w_{\mathrm{lo}})<B$, and let $w_{\mathrm{hi}}$ be the first subsequent sampled weight with $U(w_{\mathrm{hi}})\ge B$. If both exist, the solver reports $(w_{\mathrm{lo}},w_{\mathrm{hi}}]$. Its closed enclosure $[w_{\mathrm{lo}},w_{\mathrm{hi}}]$ contains the population threshold provided the grid misses no crossing, either between samples or beyond its final point. The enclosure is closed because the threshold can equal $w_{\mathrm{lo}}$ when usage rises immediately after it. The bracket's width measures grid resolution, not uncertainty, and its interior weights need not attain $B$. Without straddling endpoints, the solver flags its fallback as unbracketed, even if an unsampled population crossing exists.

\emph{Endpoint mixture.} For straddling endpoints, choose $w_{\mathrm{hi}}$ independently at the start of each episode with probability
\[
q=\frac{B-U(w_{\mathrm{lo}})}{U(w_{\mathrm{hi}})-U(w_{\mathrm{lo}})},
\]
and otherwise choose $w_{\mathrm{lo}}$, retaining that policy for the episode. Linearity gives expected usage exactly $B$ for these population endpoint usages. This is one randomized policy, not an interval of scalar prices or a constrained-reward optimum. It attains gap targets that no single weight can, consistent with the need for randomization in constrained MDPs and POMDPs \citep{altman1999,kim2011cpomdp}.
\end{definition}

In practice, the grid and mixture probability use estimated usages, so held-out usage need not equal $B$. Offline solving also labels the nearest grid point as achieving the target when $|U(w)-B|\le\max(0.3,0.1B)$. This numerical tolerance affects only that achievability label, never the bracket.

The closure of usages attainable by per-episode mixtures is $[\inf_{w\ge0}U(w),\sup_{w\ge0}U(w)]$. Every interior target can be attained by mixing two straddling members. A boundary target is attained only if that endpoint usage is attained by a member. The selected crossing mixture is more restrictive: it requires the solver's upward-straddling pair. For example, a curve that descends from usage $2$ to $1$ admits a mixture at $B=1.5$ but has no crossing from below. A curve whose final grid point falls below $B$ also gives an unbracketed fallback, even if an earlier upward crossing exists. No swept curve exhibits that final-grid shape.

All reported endpoint mixtures have straddling brackets. Tiger's $B=4$ in Table~\ref{tab:collapse-breadth} and the below-range targets of Section~\ref{sec:budget_frontier} are explicitly unbracketed. The attainable range need not begin at $U(0)$: usage is nonmonotone, and on Tileworld-$6{\times}6$ it falls from $15.64$ at $w=0$ to $14.75$ at $w=1$ (Section~\ref{sec:tileworld}). Positive $U(0)$ reflects instrumental sensing under the planner's model, while belief saturation and the episode cap limit usage at large weights.
notes: Use the same exact replacement in both live masters.
The finite-upward-crossings hypothesis excludes pathological infinitely recrossing curves while covering the finite capped discrete policy families studied.
Adds the explicit empirical-estimation distinction: equality is exact for population endpoint usages, not guaranteed by fitted calibration means.
Replaces the ambiguous endpoint attainability iff/up-to-closure sentence by separate closure, interior, and boundary statements.
The mixture formula is valid whenever endpoints straddle, including a target also attained by some other weight. This states the general linearity fact already used by the implementation.
After empirical integration, add the new B=2 failure alongside existing unbracketed examples if desired; do not imply it is the only failure.
